insights.headline: Gold steadies near $3,576 after Wednesday's wild rebound; silver back above $41
insights.summary: Spot gold held near $3,576 an ounce in early Thursday trade after recovering from $3,426 on Wednesday, while silver steadied above $41 after touching $38.09, as easing Treasury yields and a Wall Street rebound offset hot US PCE inflation of 3.8% and GDP revised up to 4.3%. MCX gold closed near Rs 1,20,429 per 10 g with silver near Rs 1,40,797 per kg. The Fed's Beige Book showed growth at a slight-to-moderate pace with sticky prices, keeping a December hike near-certain, while the rupee's eight-month high softens the blow for Indian buyers.
points: Spot gold steadied near $3,576.30, up 0.6%, after Wednesday's range of $3,426.40 to $3,590.
Silver held above $41 at about $41.12, up 0.78%, after falling as low as $38.09 in the session.
MCX gold closed near Rs 1,20,429 per 10 g and silver near Rs 1,40,797 per kg; gold is down about 13% in November.
India's gold imports fell 40% to $24.7 billion in April-October, saving $16.46 billion, trade body CTI said.
The Fed's Beige Book showed slight-to-moderate growth with sticky prices; a December hike stays near-certain.

brief.headline: Gold steadies after wild rebound; Fed hike bets stay firm
brief.summary: Gold held near $3,576 and silver above $41 after the rebound on easing yields, with MCX gold near Rs 1,20,429 per 10 g.

bullets.text: Kitco says easing Treasury yields and a Wall Street rebound steadied metals after hot PCE at 3.8% and GDP at 4.3% kept hike bets firm.
The rupee hit an eight-month high, softening the blow for Indian buyers, while gold imports fell 40% to $24.7 billion in April-October.
US markets are shut for Thanksgiving, so trading is thin; the next data is the ISM manufacturing PMI on Dec 1.

trending.title: Gold's wild Wednesday: below $3,500, then back above $3,570
trending.summary: Gold fell to $3,426, its lowest since September 2025, on hot PCE and strong GDP, then recovered toward $3,590 as yields eased and the dollar slipped.

trending.title: Silver slides further and faster, then bounces
trending.summary: Silver crashed through $40 to as low as $38.09 before rebounding above $41 late in the session; on MCX, silver is down about 20% in November.

trending.title: Fed hike bets keep bullion under pressure
trending.summary: PCE at 3.8% and core PCE at 3.3%, GDP revised up to 4.3%, and a Beige Book showing sticky prices have markets pricing a December Fed hike as near-certain, with the Dec. 8-9 meeting the next focus.

trending.title: India's imports shrink as prices ease
trending.summary: Gold imports fell 40% to $24.7 billion in April-October, saving $16.46 billion, while the RBI now holds 84% of its gold at home and the rupee sits at an eight-month high.

trending.title: Tariff proposal and a firm rupee shape the India picture
trending.summary: A US tariff proposal for 14 economies including India pressured bullion, while the rupee hit an eight-month high and closed at 92.23 per dollar on record foreign inflows into Indian equities.

items.title: Gold, silver reverse early losses as Wall Street rebounds ahead of Thanksgiving
items.summary: Spot gold recovered above $3,570 an ounce after falling below $3,450, and silver rebounded above $41, Kitco reports, as falling Treasury yields and a Wall Street rebound steadied metals despite hot PCE inflation of 3.8% and GDP revised up to 4.3%. Spot gold traded near $3,576.30, up 0.6%, after ranging from $3,426.40 to $3,590; silver traded near $41.12, up 0.78%, after falling as low as $38.09.

items.title: Gold Sinks Below $3500 as Silver Crashes Thru' $40
items.summary: Gold sank to $3,455 an ounce and silver crashed through $40 to as low as $38.68 after US GDP was revised up to 4.3% and core PCE came in at 3.3%. Markets still put a 98% chance on a quarter-point Fed hike in December. Strategist Nicky Shiels calls the sell-off a structural exit in gold, while ex-fund manager Charlie Morris sees a correction within a bull market.

items.title: India Bullion: Fall to lowest in over a year; US tariff proposal weighs
items.summary: Gold and silver futures on MCX and COMEX fell further, Informist Media reports, as a stronger dollar and rate-hike bets weighed after US inflation data matched forecasts. MCX December gold closed down 1.6% at Rs 1,20,429 per 10 g and silver down 3.2% at Rs 1,40,797 per kg, while COMEX silver touched a near-15-month low of $39.56. A US tariff plan for 14 economies, including India, also weighed.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: Fed Rate Hike Outlook Keeps Sellers in Control
items.summary: FXEmpire's analyst says silver is trying to steady early Thursday after Wednesday's sell-off broke below the October 2025 bottom at $45.55, with the analyst watching the $41.14 area as the next main bottom; the bias stays down while Fed hike expectations support the dollar and Treasury yields, though a pause in the dollar's rally may let sellers take profits.

items.title: India Records 40% Decline in Gold Imports to $24.7 Billion in April-October 2026
items.summary: India's gold imports fell 40% to $24.7 billion in April-October from $41.24 billion a year earlier, saving $16.46 billion, trade body CTI said, with October alone down 62.6% to $5.51 billion; full-year imports are estimated at $35-40 billion versus about $72 billion in FY26, and gold prices have eased to about Rs 1.25 crore per kg from Rs 1.90 crore.

items.title: Fed survey shows continued growth and sticky inflation in recent weeks
items.summary: The Fed's Beige Book found growth at a slight-to-moderate pace across most of the US, with eight of 12 districts growing, while prices rose moderately and employment increased; contacts expect costs and prices to keep rising, and markets still price at least a quarter-point hike at the Dec. 8-9 meeting after PCE came in at 3.8% and core PCE at 3.3%.

items.title: Gold's 38% Collapse Exposes the Cost of Higher Interest Rates
items.summary: Spot gold fell 3.1% to $3,446.06 an ounce, below $3,500 for the first time since September 2025 and 38% under its late-January record of $5,589.38, Investing.com reports. Markets priced a 98% chance of a December Fed hike after core PCE came in at 3.3% and Q3 GDP was revised up to 4.3%, while gold failed as a safe haven as the Nasdaq fell over 4% on forced selling.

items.title: Gold price tracker, Nov 25: COMEX gold declines 2.2%, silver tumbles 4% as US PCE inflation jumps to 3.8%
items.summary: COMEX gold fell 2.2% and silver 4% after US PCE inflation came in at 3.8% for October, with core PCE at 3.3%. MCX gold futures traded near Rs 1,20,637 per 10 g, down 1.4%, and silver near Rs 1,41,524 per kg, down 2.7%. The rupee strengthened to a 2026 high of 92.16 per dollar, softening the blow for Indian buyers.

items.title: PCE Inflation Rises to 3.8% as Stocks, Gold and Silver Weaken
items.summary: US PCE inflation rose 3.8% over the year to October, matching forecasts, while core PCE rose 3.3%, above the 3.2% expected. Both rose 0.3% on the month. Stocks fell after the release and gold and silver hit new lows for the day, with the dollar slightly weaker.

items.title: Gold prices drop another 1% as US Q3 GDP revised to 4.3% with contained PCE inflation
items.summary: US third-quarter GDP was revised up to 4.3% from the 3.4% advance estimate, Kitco reports, with the price index for gross domestic purchases up 2.7%. Spot gold fell to $3,484.20 an ounce, down nearly 2% on the day, as the strong growth data gives the Federal Reserve room to raise rates in December.

items.title: Yen, Swiss franc gain as dollar slips in volatile AI-driven session
items.summary: The dollar slipped late in a volatile session as AI-linked stocks tumbled and then clawed back most of their losses, Mint reports, with the dollar index down 0.22% at 103.62. The safe-haven yen and Swiss franc gained, and the euro rose 0.17% to $1.0983. US markets are closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving. A softer dollar eases one of the headwinds on gold after the metal's slide below $3,500.

items.title: MCX rates: Gold crashes 13%, silver plunges 20% in Nov 2026; is worst over? What should precious metals investors do?
items.summary: MCX gold has fallen about 13% in November and silver nearly 20%, pressured by a firm dollar, higher US yields and unwinding long positions. On Wednesday, MCX gold opened near ₹1,22,035 per 10 g and silver near ₹1,45,137 per kg. Analysts cited call both metals deeply oversold; the Silver Institute still sees a 35-million-ounce deficit this year, while Deutsche Bank sees a possible surplus in 2027.

items.title: Gold, silver prices decline on MCX as investors reassess outlook for US interest rates
items.summary: MCX December gold fell to an intraday low of ₹1,20,575 per 10 g and was last seen at ₹1,20,684, down 1.34%, while December silver slipped to ₹1,42,907 per kg, down 1.74%, India TV reports. Spot gold was $3,522.36 an ounce as investors reassessed the outlook for US interest rates ahead of US PCE data.

items.title: Gold, silver prices trade lower as Fed rate-hike expectations strengthen
items.summary: MCX gold opened at ₹1,22,035 per 10 g, down ₹294, and silver at ₹1,45,137 per kg, down ₹301, with Comex gold near $3,550 an ounce. Business Standard reports traders price a 96.4% chance of a December Fed hike, with US PCE data due later on Wednesday.

items.title: Gold, Silver Lose Shine: Yellow Metal Prices Fall Below Rs 1,21,000; White Metal Rates Under Rs 1,42,000
items.summary: MCX December gold fell ₹1,753, or 1.43%, to ₹1,20,576 per 10 g and silver dropped ₹2,734, or 1.88%, to ₹1,42,704 per kg, NDTV Profit reports, with both metals below the previous session's lows as traders price a December Fed hike ahead of US inflation data.

items.title: Gold falls by ₹3,635/10 gm to ₹1.21 lakh/10 gm: Silver falls by ₹9,103/kg to ₹1.43 lakh/kg
items.summary: IBJA rates show 10 g of 24-carat gold fell ₹3,635 to ₹1.21 lakh and 1 kg of silver fell ₹9,103 to ₹1.43 lakh, a 13-month low, Bhaskar English reports. Gold was ₹1.25 lakh and silver ₹1.53 lakh on November 23.

items.title: Silver futures decline to ₹1.44 lakh/kg
items.summary: MCX silver futures for December delivery fell ₹1,184, or 0.81%, to ₹1,44,254 per kg, BusinessLine reports, with global silver at $40.70 an ounce in New York, down 0.40%.

items.title: Silver Prices Fall as Hawkish Fed Signals Build Ahead of U.S. PCE Inflation Data
items.summary: Silver settled 5.69% lower at ₹1,45,438 per kg, down ₹8,779, as hawkish Fed signals built ahead of US PCE inflation data. Kedia Advisory cites a 93.5% chance of a December hike; Metals Focus forecasts global silver demand falling 5% to 1.08 billion ounces in 2026.

items.title: Silver ETFs plunge over 5%, gold ETFs fall nearly 3% as bullion prices extend losses while stock markets rally
items.summary: Silver ETFs fell up to 5.6% and gold ETFs nearly 3% on Wednesday even as the Sensex rallied 1.7%, tracking the slide in bullion on Fed hike bets and tariff worries. ICICI Prudential Silver ETF fell 5.6% to Rs 143.7 and Nippon India Silver ETF 5.5%, while ICICI Prudential Gold ETF slipped 2.7%.

items.title: Rupee scales 8-month high after holiday as foreign flows to Indian equities persist
items.summary: The rupee hit an eight-month high of 92.1850 per dollar and closed 0.7% higher at 92.23, taking its November gain to 2.9%, Reuters reports. Foreign investors have poured a record $14.28 billion into Indian stocks so far this month as money rotates away from global AI-linked shares.

items.title: RBI holds 84% of India's gold reserves domestically
items.summary: The RBI held 880.52 tonnes of gold at September-end, BusinessLine reports, with 740.13 tonnes, or 84%, stored in India, up from 680.05 tonnes in March as repatriation continued. Gold's share of total foreign exchange reserves fell to 14.38% from 16.7% as reserves grew.

items.title: Pledged gold worth less as prices crash 30% from peak; gold loan NPAs nearly double, RBI cautions NBFCs
items.summary: Gold loan NPAs nearly doubled in six months, the ratio rising to 0.3% at the end of August from 0.16% in March, TransUnion CIBIL data cited in the report shows. With gold down nearly 30% from its peak near Rs 1.80 lakh, pledged gold is worth less and loan-to-value ratios are under pressure. The RBI has asked NBFCs to tighten scrutiny of gold-loan books and warned against rapid expansion.

items.title: Silver miners struggle to close persistent supply gap
items.summary: Silver mine output is set to stay flat in 2026 despite a sixth straight annual deficit, with demand forecast to exceed supply by 35 million oz, Metals Focus estimates. Primary mines supply just 26.1% of output, the rest a byproduct of other metals mines, so higher prices alone are not lifting production. Weaker solar demand could tip the market into surplus in 2027, Deutsche Bank notes.

items.title: Gold at $8,000 could signal dollar crisis: economist
items.summary: Economist Alasdair Macleod says gold could reach $8,000 an ounce within six months, not because gold has risen but because the dollar has fallen, MINING.COM reports. He warns the Federal Reserve may have to sacrifice the dollar's purchasing power to protect markets, and that a liquidity squeeze could prompt indiscriminate selling, with the risk sitting in credit rather than in gold.
